newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia dockers strike paralyzes Buenaventura port.
newsitem.headline: Colombia dockers strike paralyzes Buenaventura port.

text.p: A strike by Colombian dock workers has paralyzed all activity in the Pacific coast port of Buenaventura, private operators said Wednesday.

The action has effectively halted 60 percent of Colombia's coffee exports and all the country's sugar exports. The port also handles exports of goods manufactured in the west and southwest of the country.

The strike, which was called late Tuesday after talks between shipping companies, cargo operators and dock workers' unions collapsed, has also prevented the unloading of imports -- including vehicles and industrial inputs.

"Even though I'm a businessman, what the workers are demanding is completely fair. There are too many operators in the port and there is a lot of unfair competition. It's a dirty price war forcing down workers' wages," said Mario Fidel Cruz, manager of Asemar SA, a secondary operator which contracts workers to load cargo.

Private coffee exporters said the National Coffee Growers' Federation was advising no consignments should be directed through Buenaventura until the strike was resolved. The federation declined to comment.

Carlos Rojas, head of customs agent PAN-Servicios, sent an urgent advisory note to coffee clients, saying: "All port activities are paralyzed due to a blockade of all entrances by dock workers," the note said.
